newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cultus, Tap Oil shares fire up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cultus, Tap Oil shares fire up.

text.p: Shares in second tier oil companies, Cultus Petroleum NL and Tap Oil NL, forged ahead on Monday as investors looked for a well-priced entry into a sector buoyed by currently high comodity prices, brokers said.

Cultus shares reached a six and a half year high of A$1.43 before easing to be up eight cents at A$1.38 by 3.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), while Tap Oil shares reached a record high of 94 cents before retreating to be four cents up on the day at A$0.91.
Tap Oil shares made their debut on the Australian Stock Exchange on September 17, 1996 at 63 cents per share.

"The oil stocks continue to be strong. Cultus and Tap Oil continue to be strong in the mid-size (stocks) and that is where the action has been in the last few weeks rather than the majors," said director at Burrell and Co, Derek Bond, adding that traders were keeping a keen eye on upcoming drilling results.
"Cultus has some interesting drilling happening over the next two months which is obviously starting to excite the market."
Cultus shares closed eight cents higher at A$1.38 on turnover of 399,759 shares while Tap Oil shares closed six cents higher at A$0.93 on turnover of 1.2 million shares.
